title: Green shakshuka
summary: Eggs poached in a skillet of softened onion, zucchini and spinach — a green take on the North African tomato dish.
steps: Heat the olive oil in a 25 cm (10 in) skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5–6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and zucchini and cook 5 minutes, stirring, until the zucchini is tender.
Add the spinach a handful at a time, letting each wilt. Season with the salt and pepper and stir in the lemon juice.
Make 6 hollows in the greens and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook over low heat 6–8 minutes, until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
Scatter with mint and basil and serve with spoonfuls of coconut yogurt.
tips: Squeeze excess liquid from the spinach if using frozen, or the pan will be watery.

origin.history: Shakshuka — eggs cooked in a spiced sauce, usually of tomatoes and peppers — is a dish of the Maghreb, most often credited to Tunisia. Tunisian and Libyan Jewish communities carried it to Israel, where it became a breakfast staple. Green versions built on leafy vegetables are a modern variation.
